question:
A 63-year-old woman with a history of emphysema presents to the clinic complaining of mid-back pain.
She denies any recent injuries but notes an increase in coughing. Her vital signs are normal, with an
oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. Osteopathic structural examination reveals restricted motion of
the left ribs 4–10 during inhalation and sharp tenderness at the left sternocostal border. If muscle
energy treatment is chosen, which muscle should be targeted? Answer Choices: (A) Rectus abdominis
(B) Serratus anterior (C) Posterior scalene (D) External oblique (E) Latissimus dorsi (F) Pectoralis
major (G) Trapezius (H) Intercostal muscles (I) Scalene muscles (J) Pectoralis minor
 A. Pectoralis major
B. External oblique
C. Scalene muscles
D. Intercostal muscles
E. Serratus anterior
F. Trapezius
G. Posterior scalene
H. Rectus abdominis
I. Pectoralis minor
J. Latissimus dorsi
